headline: WEIGHT SURGERY step 3 done: scaling ×4 doubles MATH — MIT's gap stays open
lede: Our own direction, scaled to α=4 and picked on practice alone, earned its single held-out pass: 12.0% MATH accuracy, 15.0% GSM8K — double the unedited model at the same penalty window. Still 26 points short of our reproduction of MIT's edit, and the thinking-loop escape barely moved. Next experiment, already authorized and running: read MIT's written diagnosis, hand it to the unedited model as context, and see if content alone can do what their weights do.

notes.text: #1567 closed: the practice-chosen winner's one held-out row (MATH 12.0 acc / 10.0 finished, GSM8K 15.0/15.0; MIT's own checker reads 13.0/15.0) merged with rows, aggregate, ledger and regrade — and a page verdict that renders only when the artifacts say so
Scaling is real but not the answer: ×4 doubles MATH (+6.5 mean pts) and the gain survives held-out, while finished stays 10% vs the edit's 51% — escape lives elsewhere, exactly as round 1 diagnosed

The MIT regrade nearly shipped without covering the new row: its no-arg sweep crashed on practice sidecars and a forgiving `||` still stamped the done-marker — ws3check §11 now re-verifies coverage downstream of markers, plus mutants for silent-NaN gates and self-doubling appends
12 of the disclosed 20 Astra passes spent; the held-out set was scored exactly once, and no losing variant ever touched it
